name.text: Finding the mistake in a trigonometric equation

questiontext.text:
Wekesa solved \({@eqd@}\) for \(0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ\). His working has one mistake.

Step 1\({@st1@}\)
Step 2\({@st2@}\)
Step 3\({@st3@}\)
Step 4\(\cos x = {@w1@}\) or \(\cos x = {@w2@}\)
Step 5\(x \in {@setraw(wsol)@}\)

(a) Which step has the mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Write the correct set of solutions. Give angles that are not whole numbers to 1 decimal place.

\(x \in\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Check each line against the one before.

Multiplying out step 1 and collecting terms gives \({@P2@}\cos^2 x{@tm(Q2, "\\cos x")@}{@tc(R2)@} = 0\)[[if test="is(er = 1)"]], so step 2 has the wrong sign on the \(\cos x\) term. That changes the signs of both roots.[[else]], which is step 2. Steps 3 and 4 follow.[[/if]]

The correct values are \(\cos x = {@c1@}\) or \(\cos x = {@c2@}\). For each value take the calculator angle \(\alpha\) and \(360^\circ - \alpha\) (\(\cos x = 1\) gives \(0^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\); \(\cos x = -1\) gives only \(180^\circ\)).

[[if test="is(er = 2)"]]

In step 5 Wekesa wrote only the calculator angles and missed the second angle for each value.

[[/if]][[if test="is(er = 3)"]]

In step 5 Wekesa used \(180^\circ - \alpha\), which is the rule for sine, not cosine.

[[/if]]

The mistake is in step {@erstep@}. The solutions are \(x \in {@setraw(sols)@}\).

questionnote.text: ix={@ix@}, roots {@c1@}, {@c2@}, er={@er@}, error step {@erstep@}, x={@solsd@}

questiondescription.text:
Trigonometry III: finding the mistake in a solution

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.5: Find the wrong step in a worked solution of p sin^2 x + q cos x + r = 0, then give the correct solution set.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: Step 4 follows from step 3: each bracket equals 0.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="ch3"]]

Step 3 is right for the line above it: multiply out the brackets in step 3 and you get step 2 again.

[[else]][[if test="ch2"]]

Step 2 is right: multiplying out step 1 and collecting terms gives \({@st1m@}\), and changing every sign gives step 2.

[[else]]

Step 5 gives the right angles for the values of \(\cos x\) in step 4. Check the lines those values came from.

[[/if]][[/if]]

Check each of the other lines against the one before it in the same way.

truefeedback.text: That is Wekesa's answer, which carries the mistake.

Every angle you gave is a solution, but the equation has {@length(solsF)@} solutions in \(0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ\) and you gave {@length(sl)@}.[[if test="miss360"]] When \(0^\circ\) is a solution, \(360^\circ\) is one too: both ends are in the interval.[[/if]]

[[if test="is(extras = [])"]]You have every solution, but you gave at least one of them twice, to different accuracy. Give each angle once.[[else]]You have every solution, but also {@setstr(extras)@}.[[/if]][[if test="is(outside # [])"]] Angles outside \(0^\circ\) to \(360^\circ\) are not wanted: add or subtract \(360^\circ\) to bring a calculator value into the interval.[[/if]]

Each of your angles is close to a solution, but not correct to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy and round only at the end, to 1 decimal place (round up when the next digit is 5 or more).

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(resx # [])"]]

Test your angles in the equation. For the left side of the equation, {@resstr@}. A solution gives \(0\).

[[/if]]

Correct the mistake, then solve each equation \(\cos x = k\) with \(-1 \le k \le 1\): the calculator angle \(\alpha\) and \(360^\circ - \alpha\).

[[if test="is(outside # [])"]]

Angles outside \(0^\circ\) to \(360^\circ\) are not wanted: add or subtract \(360^\circ\) to bring a calculator value into the interval.

[[/if]][[if test="radn"]]

All your values are small: check that your calculator is in degree mode, and give angles in degrees.

[[/if]]

qtest.description: Step 2 or step 5, whichever is right
Invalid: a letter in the set
